text: We evaluated a weak-to-strong generalization setup in which a qwen2.5-7b strong student is trained on labels from a gpt2-large weak supervisor, with the intervention being the discarding of examples where weak supervisors disagree, using a minimum agreement threshold of 0.8. Across 16 seeds, the weak supervisor reached 0.65 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.93, while the student trained on the filtered labels achieved a transfer accuracy of 0.67 (SE 0.02). The resulting performance gap recovered was 0.08 with a standard error of 0.08, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.23. The filtering method therefore does not recover more of the gap than the unfiltered baseline in this setting; the measured PGR falls below it, and the large standard error relative to the point estimate means the PGR itself is poorly determined. These numbers provide no evidence that agreement-based filtering improves weak-to-strong transfer here, and the single model pair limits generality.
